circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One location, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit, located around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year along with various supporting racing events. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 licence and operates as a temporary street circuit for these competitions.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Styria, the 4. 326-kilometer circuit in Austria originally operated as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix annually between 1970 and 1987. Following reconstruction and renaming to the A1-Ring, the venue resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital positioned along Baku Boulevard, spanning 6. 003 km to rank as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before being renamed and permanently established on the calendar as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that opened in 2004 and became the location for the Middle East's inaugural Formula One race that year. The facility hosts various motorsport events including GP2 racing and endurance competitions, while operating under FIA Grade 1 classification with alternative track configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple driver skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in Belgium's Wallonia region, Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km circuit that has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix since 1925 and participated in Formula One's inaugural season in 1950. The venue has maintained an almost continuous Grand Prix calendar presence from 1985 onward, with only brief absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km track that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its primary role hosting the sport's elite series, the circuit has accommodated various international racing competitions including sports car championships and North American touring series over the years.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese racing facility served as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 through 2019 before resuming the event from 2024 onward. The venue additionally began hosting electric racing competition from 2024 onwards, expanding its motorsport calendar beyond its traditional Formula One fixture.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, located near villages in Northamptonshire, England, serves as the permanent home of the British Grand Prix since 1987 and held the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. The track had previously rotated hosting duties with two other circuits between 1955 and 1986, though it first staged the British Grand Prix in 1948. Beyond Formula One, the circuit also accommodates MotoGP competition.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the first Formula One circuit in Eastern Europe when it hosted the Hungarian Grand Prix in 1986, remarkable for being constructed in just eight months. Located outside the city rather than in Budapest's central park as originally considered, this 4. 381 km track was built following Bernie Ecclestone's interest in establishing a race behind the Iron Curtain, with the inaugural event dedicated to Hungarian motorsport pioneer János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Situated near Monza in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, the track has earned its nickname "the Temple of Speed" from its extended straights and fast-cornering layout.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The 5. 807-kilometre Suzuka Circuit in Mie Prefecture, Japan, stands as a premier motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track has become synonymous with Formula One racing and serves as the host circuit for the Japanese Grand Prix, establishing itself as one of the sport's most iconic destinations.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that weaves through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous boulevard lined with major hotels and casino resorts. The track features iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it navigates the heart of the Strip's entertainment district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, a 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City, honors two Mexican racing brothers who died in motorsport accidents. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's premier race in 2015 after a 23-year absence, though on its current track layout rather than the configuration used during previous hosting periods ending in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that measures 3. 363 miles with 19 turns and generates qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Developed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One use, the venue joined the championship calendar in 2022 as the home of the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix takes place on a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the coastal harbour layout of the principality. Although officially named Circuit de Monaco, it is widely known as Monte Carlo since the majority of the track occupies that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: This 4. 259 km Dutch motorsport venue in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix starting in 2021, though the arrangement will conclude after 2026. The track, situated north of Zandvoort close to the North Sea, operates under a sponsorship naming agreement that took effect in mid-2025.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419 km track featuring a notably long main straight of over 1 km. Holding an FIA Grade 1 license, the facility incorporates artificial grass around its perimeter as a protective measure against sand intrusion into the racing surface.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing venue in São Paulo, Brazil, originally opened in 1940 and later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aviation accident. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and houses an additional kart facility dedicated to Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Jeddah's waterfront adjacent to the Red Sea, hosting the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since 2021.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: Singapore's Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through the Downtown Core and Kallang districts, forming a unique urban racing venue centered around the waterfront area of Marina Bay.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this Spanish racing venue stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a well-balanced layout combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing overall vehicle performance. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate nearly 141,000 spectators.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: COTA is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA circuit situated in Austin, Texas, that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. The venue accommodates multiple racing series including NASCAR, MotoGP, and the FIA World Endurance Championship, though it has previously hosted various other motorsport categories across different eras.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: A Thai-British racing driver, Alexander Albon represents Thailand in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world titles during his 23-season career with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours wins and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both a Formula One championship and a world sportscar title.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes in Formula One, having secured six race victories following his entry into the championship in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, where he competes at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabriel Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One, representing Audi in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish competitor, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One. The driver achieved two runner-up finishes in the championship standings during his Mercedes years in 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his 13-season career in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One with the Alpine team, representing his country in the sport's premier racing series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve position with the Haas Formula One team while competing in European Le Mans Series endurance racing. He has made seven Grand Prix appearances during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a significant highlight of his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: French-Algerian driver Isack Alexandre Hadjar races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding an impressive seven world championship titles that he shares with Michael Schumacher. The accomplished competitor holds multiple records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, notably winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand-born racing driver, currently competes in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: A driver from Monaco, Leclerc has established himself as a competitive force in Formula One with Ferrari, achieving nine race victories since joining the grid. He came close to the championship title in 2022, finishing as runner-up in the drivers' standings during his tenure with the Italian team.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, who raced in Formula One across two separate stints from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024, currently competes as a factory driver for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT. He also maintains a part-time presence in NASCAR's top series, piloting the No. 91 Chevrolet for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Over his eight-season career, he has accumulated 12 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon currently races for Haas in Formula One, having previously claimed a race victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix during his time with Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver competing for Cadillac, finished second in the 2023 championship while racing for Red Bull. Over 15 seasons in Formula One, he has claimed six race victories.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his career. He achieved eight Grand Prix victories across his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British driver, currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories during his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes in Formula One for Williams and has claimed four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, following his previous involvement in IMSA's LMP2 division with Era Motorsport. His Formula One career spanned the 2023 and 2024 seasons.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor who currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda held a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls during his Formula One involvement from 2021 to 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen, a Dutch-Belgian driver racing under the Dutch flag, has claimed four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles from 2021 to 2024 while competing for Red Bull Racing. Across 12 seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently working as a reserve driver for the Cadillac Formula One team. He competed in the championship from 2022 to 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have raced in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Since 2021, the Enstone-based outfit has raced as Alpine F1, Renault's rebranding of its works team to showcase the sports car marque. The squad secured a single victory in its Alpine identity when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, before Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025. Now powered by Mercedes engines, the team operates under a French licence and currently fields Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has appeared in Formula One under different configurations throughout the sport's history, with the current incarnation operating as AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury automaker and stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished competitor, having participated in every world championship since the sport's inception in 1950. The team, nicknamed after their distinctive emblem, has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the championship's entire history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas, a NASCAR team owner, founded this American-licensed Formula One outfit in 2014, with the squad beginning competition in 2016. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm established itself as a dominant endurance racing competitor, notably winning the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours alongside Mercedes-Benz. The organization entered Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor and competed for over three decades, becoming the sport's fourth-longest-running team by race entries before ceasing operations in 2025, when Audi acquired it to serve as the foundation for its factory F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technology facility in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group, which is owned by Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954, functioning as both a constructor and engine supplier throughout its involvement in the sport. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas team operates from Brackley under a German licence, with ownership restructured in 2022 to include equal stakes held by the Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The marque's racing entries are traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's second constructor entry in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor based in Faenza that entered the grid in 2024 as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH, alongside Red Bull Racing. The squad maintains a secondary facility in Milton Keynes close to its sister team's headquarters.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has been a prominent Formula One competitor since its 2005 establishment under Red Bull GmbH ownership. Led by Christian Horner throughout its two-decade tenure before Laurent Mekies assumed leadership in 2025, the team operates as one of two Formula One entries controlled by the Red Bull conglomerate.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering stands as a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's prior failed racing venture. Operating from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team.
